title: GPU pool eviction patterns — lab notes and quick timeline
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad while triaging repeated evictions / capacity flapping in a dedicated GPU pool (us-west-2-dedicated-1). Goal is to capture commands, raw snippets, hypotheses, and next steps so I (and others) don't re-run the same blind experiments. NOT an official postmortem — leaning toward notes-to-self and breadcrumbs.

Observed symptom summary:
- Multiple apps reported cold-starts + token latency spikes ~09/12–09/14 causing user-facing timeouts (200–500ms -> 2–4s tails).
- Pool size reported as stable in console but nodes were repeatedly BNI-evicted then reattached (observed 3x/day).
- Autoscaler logs show scale-down events that coincide with unhealthy warmup counts.
- Critical: GPU utilization on renewed nodes is low for first ~90s then jumps — suggests warm-cache / model loading lag, not kernel-level issue.

Timeline (rough):
- 2025-09-12 03:17 UTC: first alert from routing that 95th latency exceeded SLO by 1.8x (trace id 0xafe3).
- 2025-09-12 03:19 UTC: infra autoscaler scale-down executed target 14 -> 10 (policy: aggressive-burst), reason: low avg_cpu across nodes.
- 2025-09-12 03:21 UTC: multiple nodes rotated; kubelet reported: "NodeMarkedForDeletion" then "EvictionReason: NodeCapacityPrune" logs.
- 2025-09-13 11:02 UTC: customer SLA report — two 30s+ tail latencies.

Commands I ran (keep these):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels | grep dedicated-1
  -> saw nodes with labels: dedicated=true, prewarm=false, gpu-type=A100x2

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-3-45.us-west-2.internal
  -> Conditions: Ready False  (LastHeartbeatTime: 2025-09-12T03:20:14Z)
  -> Events: "Killing pods due to NodeShutdown" then "Node has been marked for deletion by autoscaler"

- kubectl logs -n infra autoscaler-0 --since=6h | grep -i "scale-down" -n
  -> 2025-09-12T03:18:52Z "scaleDown: removing node ip-10-0-3-45" (reason: low-reservation)

- gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output ip-10-0-3-45 --zone=us-west2-a | tail -n 120
  -> kernel: "GPU0: device ready" then 30s silence then "nv_ml_model_loader: model load complete"

- curl -s "https://internal-metrics/api/v1/query?query=gpu_warm_seconds_avg"
  -> returned histogram; bin[0-30s] high count for 09/12–09/14.

Observed error snippets (raw-ish):
- kubelet: "failed to cleanup pod sandbox: error removing network namespace: file exists" (retries 6) — maybe CNI timing with node delete?
- autoscaler: "node did not become ready in threshold, marking for deletion" -- threshold was 45s (policy config).
- model-server logs: "KV-cache-miss: prefix not present for session X" and repeated model load fallbacks.

Hypotheses so far (ranked):
1) Aggressive scale-down policy + short node-ready threshold (45s) -> nodes removed before they finish pre-loading models, causing clients to be routed away and then back, triggering warm churn. Evidence: autoscaler logs + gcloud serial timing.
2) Prewarm flag not applied consistently to newly created nodes due to cloud-init race with instance metadata; some nodes come up labeled prewarm=false, autoscaler sees low util and deletes them quickly. Evidence: label inspection showed mixture.
3) CNI / kubelet race during node reattachment causing pod network not to be ready; network failure triggers additional pod restarts which look like capacity thrash. Evidence: network namespace errors in kubelet.
4) Model load is taking longer because of quantized kernel selection path regression introduced in infra PR #867 — causes unstable warm durations. Evidence: correlated PR in linked artifacts and model-server logs mention kernel selection path.

Quick experiments attempted (and results):
- Increased node-ready threshold to 120s (cluster autoscaler config, patch applied 2025-09-13 02:00 UTC) — short term reduction in churn but cost increased; tail latencies reduced but not eliminated.
- Forcing prewarm annotation on new pools via startup script (testing on staging) — staging nodes came up with prewarm=true and model loads completed consistently in ~28s vs 62s without flag. Promising.
- Disabled aggressive-burst policy for one AZ; no churn observed for 6 hours but can't roll globally yet.
- Rolled back infra PR 867 in a canary pool (manually pinned older runtime) — warm durations returned to prior baseline (~20–30s) in that canary. Strong signal pointing to PR regression.

Data to check / graphs to produce next: (todo)
- Per-node "time from instance-ready to first successful inference" for last 7 days (group by image tag & cloud-init version).
- Distribution of node labels on creation events (prewarm=true/false) vs. instance metadata.
- Autoscaler decision traces (why it flagged nodes for removal) around time of each deletion.
- Correlate PR 867 rollout timeline with warm-duration percentiles.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- (Priya) Bake a small synthetic load that polls model endpoint right after node attach to measure warm success time precisely; run against canary pool. Deadline: 2025-09-16.
- (Ethan) Re-run cloud-init with logging enabled on new instances to capture metadata race. Attach logs to JIRA INF-5129. Deadline: 2025-09-15.
- (Maya) Prepare rollback checklist for PR 867 across dedicated pools; include canary window and metrics guard rails. Deadline: 2025-09-15 EOD.

Longer-term ideas / mitigations:
- Make prewarm an enforced label via instance template (avoid cloud-init race).
- Autoscaler: add a "warm-up-exempt" grace period where nodes with prewarm=true are not considered for scale-down for X sec.
- Model server: expose a readiness probe that only passes after KV-cache has at least N prefixes loaded to prevent routing traffic to "cold" node. (Implementation tradeoffs: readiness might block capacity accounting.)
- Add metric for "first-inference-latency-per-node" and alert if median>target for new nodes.

Notes/reflections:
- We have classic control-loop instability: aggressive down-scaling + variable warm durations -> oscillation.
- Quick fix that reduced customer pain was increasing node-ready-threshold + pinning the canary to older runtime. But this is costly; need a safer long-term solution.

Raw snippets appended below (copy-paste friendly):
--- kubectl describe node snippet ---
Name:           ip-10-0-3-45.us-west-2.internal
Labels:         dedicated=us-west-2-dedicated-1, gpu-type=A100x2, prewarm=false
Conditions:
  Type    Status  LastHeartbeatTime
  Ready   False   2025-09-12T03:20:14Z
Events:
  03:18:52Z  Normal  NodeIsTerminating  Node has been marked for deletion by autoscaler

--- kubelet error sample ---
E0912 03:20:18.472123  1234 kubelet.go:203] failed to cleanup pod sandbox: error removing network namespace /proc/4567/ns/net: file exists

--- autoscaler log line ---
2025-09-12T03:18:52Z INFO autoscaler: scaleDown: removing node ip-10-0-3-45 reason=low-reservation nodeReadyDuration=22s

--- model server warm log ---
[2025-09-12T03:20:00Z] nv_ml: model loader start
[2025-09-12T03:20:23Z] nv_ml: kernel-selector: chosen kernel v2.14-quantized
[2025-09-12T03:20:55Z] nv_ml: model load complete (elapsed 55s)

If anything is stale here, ping me in #infra-warmup and I will archive/refine. Will convert to a formal postmortem if we confirm PR regression is root cause.

-- Priya
